text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.67% today, closing at $154.03, as crude oil prices surged on geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Reports of escalating Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global oil—pushed crude toward $123 per barrel globally, and the prospect of U.S.-Iran negotiations breaking down kept that pressure on. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher oil prices directly translate to higher revenues and profits from production.

The move also reflects a broader tailwind: refineries across the sector are reporting surging earnings as fuel supplies have tightened, which benefits both upstream producers and their downstream operations. This contrasts sharply with political pressure—Trump has called out Big Oil for excessive profits—but market mechanics are favoring energy companies regardless.
